title: Failover controller: add dry-run mode (recommendations + audit events, no execution)
author: Benji Okafor
description: This PR introduces a first-class dry-run mode for the regional failover controller. In dry-run, the controller evaluates current region signals and routing policy state, computes the recommended policy flips (failover / partial shift / no-op), and emits a structured audit event describing the decision and evidence signals, but it does not execute any routing changes or drain actions. Motivation: we need a safe way to validate trigger hierarchy + policy evaluation end-to-end (including dashboards/alerts and incident-bot hooks) before enabling automation in production. This is a prerequisite for the Q1 2026 controlled failover game day and for gradually rolling out automation behind feature flags. Scope: controller behavior + config + audit event emission + metrics. Out of scope: the actual execution path (policy flips), approval hooks, and rollback semantics (tracked separately). Design notes: (1) Dry-run is controlled via config flag failover_controller.mode = "dry_run" (default remains "disabled" in prod, "enabled" only via explicit Helm values). (2) The recommender uses the deterministic signal evaluation API from policy engine (see PR #19812) and the region health aggregator client (see PR #19810) when present; missing signals are treated as "unknown" and surfaced in the output for operator visibility (no implicit failover on unknown in dry-run). (3) Recommendations are returned via an internal endpoint and also logged periodically (rate limited) with a stable decision hash to support correlation and avoid log spam. (4) Audit events are written to the existing audit sink with event_type=failover.recommendation so downstream tooling can render and annotate dashboards without requiring that a real failover occurred. Acceptance criteria for ENG-2415: - Operators can enable dry-run in staging and see computed recommended actions with evidence. - No routing policy writes occur in dry-run (asserted via unit tests + integration test with a fake policy store). - An audit event is emitted for every recommendation cycle and includes region, route scope, recommended action, trigger(s), and decision hash. - Metrics reflect recommendation cycles and "would have flipped" counts to help tune thresholds without customer impact. Testing: added unit tests for mode gating and write suppression; added an integration test running the controller against a fake signal stream and verifying audit emission; ran staging deploy with dry-run enabled for /v1/chat routes only and confirmed no config writes. Rollout: land behind flag; staging config pack will enable dry-run by default; production remains disabled until go/no-go.
commits: failover-controller: add Mode enum and dry-run plumbing
controller: split recommendation vs execution paths (no-op executor for dry-run)
audit: emit failover.recommendation events with evidence + decision hash
tests: ensure no policy writes occur in dry-run
docs: update controller README with dry-run usage and examples
changed_files: deploy/helm/redwood/values.yaml (document mode flag; default remains disabled)
review_conversation: Miles Thornton (review): The recommender/executor split looks good. Can we guarantee no writes at all in dry-run, including incidental "touch" calls to the policy store? Also please include the specific trigger evidence we used (reachability / 5xx burn / latency burn / capacity) in the event payload so game day observers can debug why the recommendation happened. Benji Okafor (author): Added a strict interface for PolicyStore where write methods are not even constructed in dry-run (dependency injection picks NoopExecutor + ReadOnlyPolicyStore). Added unit test that fails if any write method is invoked. Also expanded evidence to include signal snapshot with "unknown" markers. Ravi Menon (review): For the decision hash, ensure stable ordering of evidence keys; otherwise we will churn hashes and spam audit. Also rate limit audit emission; we only need it on decision change or every N minutes. Benji Okafor (author): Implemented deterministic canonical JSON serialization for decision hash input and added an emission policy: emit on decision change, plus a heartbeat every 10 minutes. Allison Grant (review): Metrics labels: please avoid route_id/cardinality explosions. Use coarse dimensions (tier, region, action, trigger_primary). Benji Okafor (author): Switched to bounded labels and added a comment on cardinality constraints. Ethan Park (review): Internal endpoint should be auth-protected; ensure it’s only reachable from the ops network / service-to-service auth. Benji Okafor (author): Hooked into existing internal auth middleware and restricted to "ops" service identity. Final: Miles approved after verifying the write-suppression test and the audit payload fields.
release_notes: Internal-only: adds failover controller dry-run mode to compute and report recommended regional failover actions without executing routing changes; includes audit events and low-cardinality metrics to support controlled failover validation.
